observation: Dense checkpoint MLPs are copied into experts, router newly initialized, then training continues. More experts can raise initial loss; randomly initialized experts recover slowly; Gaussian noise diversification did not help. Language experiments use T5 encoder-decoder and continued pretraining, not cheap CPU conversion.

Fine-grained donor MLP sharding plus replication needs virtual groups selecting one copy of every shard and weight scaling to preserve initial forward behavior. Naive sharding/replication produced high loss. 2B ablations use 110B tokens; 15B final uses 1T; authors report reduced GPU FLOP utilization for higher granularity.

Drop-Upcycling partially reinitializes aligned SwiGLU intermediate columns across gate/up/down matrices. Retained representation and specialization trade off; zero reset fraction gives less long-run gain, 0.75 or 1.0 impedes donor transfer. Requires substantial training and changes exact donor function.

MoEfication partitions donor FFN neurons and trains a selector on activation labels; all selected experts reconstruct original FFN. T5/BERT ReLU tasks retained >95% relative downstream scores using 10-30% FFN parameters, with roughly 500k router representations; T5-Large decoder MLP selection accuracy reported near 0.7. Results are task/model-specific and do not establish Falcon free-running quality or CPU wall time.

Deja Vu predicts contextual sparse heads/MLP from nearby layer states and overlaps lookahead with accelerator execution. OPT-175B >2x versus FasterTransformer on 8 A100s; the paper explicitly separates existence, prediction and hardware efficiency, and notes unstructured sparsity need not accelerate wall time.

PowerInfer hot/cold neuron split uses GPU residency and CPU cold execution. Predictors were 4.88-8.68% of original model parameters for listed models and placed preferentially on GPU. SiLU model speedups 1.47-1.7x, CPU can bottleneck; quantized RTX4090 average 13.20 and peak 29.08 tokens/s across evaluated models. These numbers cannot certify CPU-only Ryzen target.

DeepSeekMoE always-on shared experts absorb common knowledge, while finer routed experts specialize; shared experts replace routed slots to hold active compute fixed. Evidence is from scratch training at 100B, 245B or 2T tokens, not donor surgery.

LLM in a Flash selectively loads predicted FFN columns/rows from flash, keeps attention resident, and favors contiguous bundled reads. Its predictor example used 10k C4 samples, 2 epochs, four hours per predictor on A100; coactivation friend bundling caused redundant hot-neuron reads. Flash constraints and timings differ from resident DRAM CPU.

SparseGPT yields 50-60% one-shot unstructured sparsity for OPT/BLOOM 175B class, and reports joint 50% sparse plus 4-bit quantization on OPT-175B with small perplexity change. This is static weight sparsity; compression or theoretical operation count alone does not prove a CPU speedup or conditional capacity.
